verdict.rationale: Svelte's docs say components are written in HTML, CSS and JavaScript. A `<script>` block holds JS or TS, and a `<style>` block is scoped to the component. Community comments confirm the single-file component approach in practice. missing for 10: a documented end-to-end example of one file combining markup, script and style, and resolution of a community-reported IDE-support caveat about the template syntax extending JavaScript.

support.subject: As a developer, I can write markup and rendering logic together in a single component using markup, styles, and a language I already know

citations.quote: write breathtakingly concise components that do minimal work in the browser, using languages you already know — HTML, CSS and JavaScript.
It uses a compiler to turn declarative components written in HTML, CSS and JavaScript...into lean, tightly optimized JavaScript.
A `<script>` block contains JavaScript (or TypeScript, when adding the `lang="ts"` attribute) that runs when a component instance is created.
CSS inside a `<style>` block will be scoped to that component.
